title_en: China Great Wall Asset Management Co., Ltd., Jilin Branch v. Jilin City Small and Medium Enterprise Credit Guarantee Group Co., Ltd. and State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of Jilin Municipal People's Government — disputes over tort liability and liability for shareholders harming company creditors' interests
ruling_gist_en: The Tort Liability Law protects the lawful personal and property rights and interests of civil subjects. A legally established and effective creditor's right constitutes the lawful property rights and interests of the creditor, is protected by law, and shall not be infringed upon at will by any person. A creditor's right arises between specific parties and lacks publicity. In general, the creditor should assert its rights through contractual remedies. The determination of a third party not a party to the contract to bear tort compensation liability shall be strictly scrutinized. When the creditor's remedies have been exhausted, and a third party external to the creditor-debtor relationship, knowing or should have known of the existence of the creditor's right, and violates laws, regulations, or other normative legal documents aimed at protecting such creditor's right, or acts contrary to public order and good customs, causing damage to the creditor's lawful rights and interests, the actor shall bear corresponding supplementary compensation liability.
keywords_en: Civil; Tort liability dispute; Dispute over liability for shareholders damaging company creditors' interests; Second instance; Supreme People's Court; Jilin Province; Legal person; State organ; Tort Liability Law; General Principles of the Civil Law; Company Law; Enterprise Bankruptcy Law; Elements of third-party infringement of creditor's rights; Whether gratuitous transfer of equity constitutes infringement; Whether bankruptcy creditors can directly claim against third parties; Partial support; Assignment of creditor's rights; Gratuitous transfer of equity; Bankruptcy claims; Guarantee liability; Public order and good customs; Tort liability; Guarantee; Dispute over tort liability of the Supervision and Management Committee; Dispute over liability for harming company creditors' interests
full_text_en:
China Great Wall Asset Management Co., Ltd. Jilin Branch v.

Jilin City Small and Medium Enterprise Credit Guarantee Group Co., Ltd.,

and

State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of Jilin Municipal People's Government

— Dispute over Tort Liability, Dispute over Liability for Damage to Company Creditors' Interests by Shareholders

【Ruling Summary】

The Tort Liability Law protects the legitimate personal and property rights and interests of civil subjects. A legally established and effective creditor's right constitutes a legitimate property right and interest of the creditor, is protected by law, and shall not be arbitrarily violated by anyone. A creditor's right arises between specific parties and lacks publicity. Generally, a creditor should assert its rights through contractual remedies. The determination of tort liability for damages against a third party outside the contractual relationship shall be strictly controlled. Where a creditor's avenues for relief have been exhausted, and a third party outside the debtor-creditor relationship, knowing or having reason to know of the existence of the debtor-creditor relationship, and violating laws, regulations, or other normative legal documents intended to protect such creditor's right, or violating public order and good customs, thereby causing damage to the creditor's legitimate rights and interests, the actor shall bear corresponding supplementary compensation liability.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Judgment

(2017) Supreme People's Court Final Civil No. 181

Appellant (Original Defendant): Jilin City Small and Medium Enterprise Credit Guarantee Group Co., Ltd. Domicile: Building B, Hongbo Jingyuan, No. 2 Wusong East Road, Changyi District, Jilin City, Jilin Province.

Legal Representative: Jiang Yongheng, Chairman of the Board.

Authorized Litigation Agent: Xiu Bao, Lawyer of Jilin Baomin Law Firm.

Authorized Litigation Agent: Chen Si, Lawyer of Jilin Xueliu Law Firm.

Appellee (Original Plaintiff): China Great Wall Asset Management Co., Ltd. Jilin Branch (formerly China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation Changchun Office). Domicile: No. 1455 Xi'an Avenue, Chaoyang District, Changchun City, Jilin Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Guoliang, General Manager of the Company.

Authorized Litigation Agent: Feng Yanjun, Lawyer of Jilin Jida Law Firm.

Authorized Litigation Agent: Mu Zhenhui, Lawyer of Beijing Zhongwen Law Firm.

Original Defendant: State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of Jilin Municipal People's Government. Domicile: No. 11 Yueshan Road, Chuanying District, Jilin City, Jilin Province.

Responsible Person: Wang Likuang, Director of the Entity.

Authorized Litigation Agent: Zhang Long, Lawyer of Jilin Baomin Law Firm.

Authorized Litigation Agent: Xiu Zhiyu, Lawyer of Beijing Bentong Law Firm.

In the case of the appeal filed by the appellant, Jilin City Small and Medium Enterprise Credit Guarantee Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as SME Guarantee Company), against the appellee, China Great Wall Asset Management Co., Ltd. Jilin Branch (hereinafter referred to as Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch), and the original defendant, State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of Jilin Municipal People's Government (hereinafter referred to as Jilin City SASAC), concerning a dispute over tort liability and a dispute over liability for damage to company creditors' interests by shareholders, the appellant, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2015) Jilin Civil First Instance No. 8 rendered by the Jilin High People's Court, appealed to this court. This court, after filing the case on March 22, 2017, formed a collegial panel according to law and held a hearing. The authorized litigation agents of the appellant, SME Guarantee Company, Xiu Bao and Chen Si, the authorized litigation agents of the appellee, Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch, Feng Yanjun and Mu Zhenhui, and the authorized litigation agents of the original defendant, Jilin City SASAC, Zhang Long and Xiu Zhiyu, appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The present case has now been concluded.

SME Guarantee Company's appeal requests: 1. To revoke the civil judgment (2015) Jilin Civil First Instance No. 8 rendered by the Jilin High People's Court according to law; 2. To dismiss all of Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch's claims at first instance according to law; 3. To have the litigation costs of the first and second instance borne by Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch. Facts and Reasons: The essence of this case is a creditor's right to avoid actions in bankruptcy. Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch should have asserted its right to avoidance in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law) and the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Contract Law). Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch maliciously circumvented the law and abused litigation rights. Without any evidence supporting its claims, it re-litigated based on Article 3 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China. The court of first instance filed the case as a contract dispute, but in its judgment, based on Article 106 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the General Principles of Civil Law), it erroneously determined that SME Guarantee Company had committed tort and ordered it to bear tort liability. Tort refers to infringement of property rights and personal rights, and does not include infringement of creditor's rights. Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch did not submit any evidence at first instance to prove what fault constituted the tortious act of SME Guarantee Company. The first instance judgment lacks factual and legal basis and should be corrected. (A) The first instance judgment violated procedural requirements. 1. The first instance court filed the case as a contract dispute, did not explain the change of cause of action during trial, but determined the cause of action as a tort liability dispute in the judgment. 2. When Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch alleged malicious collusion between SME Guarantee Company and Jilin Huaxing Electronics Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huaxing Company), the court of first instance did not add Huaxing Company as a co-defendant, violating the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law. (B) The first instance judgment found facts unclear. 1. Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch is not the injured party and does not have a basic legal relationship of tortious conduct with SME Guarantee Company. The legal connection of Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch is with Huaxing Group. Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch is a bankruptcy creditor of Huaxing Company and holds bankruptcy claims against Huaxing Company. As a bankruptcy creditor of Huaxing Company, Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch should exercise its rights in accordance with the procedures provided by the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law and participate in the distribution of Huaxing Company's bankruptcy property. 2. There was no malicious collusion between SME Guarantee Company and Huaxing Company. SME Guarantee Company had no fault and did not commit a tort. SME Guarantee Company's acquisition of the equity involved in the case was in compliance with laws and regulations. The transfer of equity between Huaxing Company and SME Guarantee Company was approved by the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council (SASAC) and the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC), and a transfer announcement was issued by the CSRC. It complied with the legal provisions and statutory procedures for the transfer of state-owned shares. (C) The first instance judgment applied the law incorrectly. The claim asserted by Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch is a creditor's right. A creditor's right is not an object of tortious conduct as defined in the General Principles of Civil Law or the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Tort Liability Law). Therefore, the above laws should not apply to this case. This is a dispute over the right to avoid bankruptcy creditor's rights, and should be governed by the Contract Law and the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law. (D) The first instance judgment objectively resulted in Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch receiving separate satisfaction. This case could lead to serious consequences such as claims by Huaxing Company's employees and other creditors, the possible bankruptcy filing by SME Guarantee Company, and damage to the legal environment and economic development in the Northeast region.

Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch argued in response: (A) This case is unrelated to a bankruptcy avoidance dispute. According to legal provisions and the actual circumstances, Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch sued SME Guarantee Company for joint and several liability. It has the right to legally choose the direction and grounds of the lawsuit based on its needs. (B) The first instance judgment did not violate procedural requirements. 1. Huaxing Company has been bankrupt and deregistered for many years; its legal personality no longer exists. The bankruptcy administrator of Huaxing Company has long completed its mission and has been formally dissolved, and is now not competent to participate in the trial of this case. 2. Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch claimed joint and several liability against SME Guarantee Company. The first instance court filed the case as a contract dispute, but after trial and in the main text of the first instance judgment, it specifically explained that this case should be for tort-based joint and several liability. The nature of the joint and several liability claimed by Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch did not change, nor did it affect SME Guarantee Company's defense. Determining the cause of action accordingly does not violate the rules. (C) SME Guarantee Company should bear joint and several liability. 1. Huaxing Company should bear civil liability for its gratuitous transfer of assets. The Supreme People's Court's civil ruling (2012) Supreme People's Court Final Civil No. 58 clearly stated that the gratuitous transfer of assets, even if approved and transferred, cannot be used as a pretext to harm the interests of creditors. Such cases should be accepted as civil cases and the responsible party should bear corresponding liability according to law. 2. SME Guarantee Company should bear joint and several liability according to law. In order to evade guarantee debts, Huaxing Company, during the period of its guarantee obligations, gratuitously transferred its equity assets to SME Guarantee Company. The transferee should bear joint and several repayment liability within the scope of the gratuitously transferred assets. (D) Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch has the right to sue the joint and several debtor and obtain direct satisfaction. 1. According to the relevant provisions of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, SME Guarantee Company and Jilin City SASAC, as joint and several debtors of Huaxing Company, even if the bankruptcy proceedings of Huaxing Company have been concluded, have the obligation to satisfy the creditor's claims. 2. The equity involved in this case does not belong to the debtor's property or bankruptcy property, but is a legitimate asset of SME Guarantee Company. Therefore, the relevant provisions of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law cannot be applied to recover and redistribute. Since SME Guarantee Company obtained the assets gratuitously, Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch may directly exercise its right of recourse against it according to law. In conclusion, it requests that the appeal of SME Guarantee Company be dismissed and the original judgment be upheld.

Jilin City SASAC stated: 1. Jilin City SASAC is not a shareholder of Huaxing Company and is not the proper defendant in a case concerning liability for damage to company creditors' interests by shareholders. 2. The bankruptcy of Huaxing Company complied with legal provisions and legal procedures. Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch's allegation that Huaxing Company used bankruptcy to evade debts has no factual or legal basis. 3. The first instance judgment caused a separate satisfaction of a bankruptcy creditor, violating relevant policies and the provisions of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, and infringing upon the rights and interests of other bankruptcy creditors, especially those with priority in satisfaction as bankruptcy creditors. It lacks factual and legal basis and should be revoked according to law.

Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance, requesting: 1. To order SME Guarantee Company, within the scope of the benefits derived from the gratuitous receipt of 20 million shares of Jilin Huamicro Electronics Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huamicro Company) held by Huaxing Company, to bear joint and several repayment liability for the principal and interest of the debt totaling RMB 209,240,000.00; 2. To order Jilin City SASAC, within the scope of its abuse of shareholder rights in the gratuitous transfer of the 20 million shares of Huamicro Company held by Huaxing Company, to bear joint and several repayment liability for the above principal and interest of the debt; 3. To have the litigation costs borne by SME Guarantee Company and Jilin City SASAC.

The court of first instance found the following facts: From 1997 to 2001, Huaxing Company, as the main debtor, provided joint and several guarantee for four debts owed by Jilin Gaote (Group) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Gaote Company), Jilin Chuangshang Hospital (hereinafter referred to as Chuangshang Hospital), the Semiconductor Branch of Jilin High-tech Industrial Development Zone Import and Export Trading Company (hereinafter referred to as the Semiconductor Branch), and Jilin Longding Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Longding Company) to the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Co., Ltd. Jilin Branch (hereinafter referred to as ICBC Jilin Branch), with principal amounts of RMB 66.63 million and USD 4.8 million, plus corresponding interest.

On July 31, 2005, ICBC Jilin Branch transferred the above four debts together to the Changchun Office of China Orient Asset Management Corporation.

On January 16, 2006, Huaxing Company submitted a "Request for Implementation of Restructuring of Jilin Huaxing Electronics Group Co., Ltd." to Jilin City SASAC, requesting: "We intend to transfer the state-owned shares of Huamicro held by our company to the municipal government for disposal, with employees to be resettled by the Jilin Municipal Government."

On February 15, 2006, Jilin City SASAC issued Document No. (2006) 29, approving Huaxing Company to "transfer the 20 million state-owned legal person shares of Jilin Huamicro Electronics Co., Ltd. held by it to the Jilin Municipal Government, which will resettle employees and pay resettlement costs."

On October 31, 2008, Jilin City SASAC submitted a "Request for Gratuitous Transfer of State-owned Legal Person Shares of Jilin Huaxing Electronics Group Co., Ltd. to Jilin City Small and Medium Enterprise Credit Guarantee Co., Ltd." (Jilin City SASAC Document (2008) No. 53) to the Jilin Municipal People's Government, requesting: "We intend to gratuitously transfer 20 million state-owned legal person shares held by Jilin Huaxing Electronics Group Co., Ltd. to Jilin City Small and Medium Enterprise Credit Guarantee Co., Ltd."

On the same day, the Jilin Municipal People's Government issued a "Reply of the Jilin Municipal People's Government Approving the Gratuitous Transfer of State-owned Legal Person Shares of Jilin Huaxing Electronics Group Co., Ltd. to Jilin City Small and Medium Enterprise Credit Guarantee Co., Ltd." (Jilin Municipal Government Document (2008) No. 265), "approving the gratuitous transfer of 20 million state-owned legal person shares held by Jilin Huaxing Electronics Group Co., Ltd. to Jilin City Small and Medium Enterprise Credit Guarantee Co., Ltd."

On November 18, 2008, Jilin City SASAC submitted a "Request for Gratuitous Transfer of State-owned Legal Person Shares of Jilin Huaxing Electronics Group Co., Ltd. to Jilin City Small and Medium Enterprise Credit Guarantee Co., Ltd." (Jilin City SASAC Document (2008) No. 58) to the Jilin Provincial SASAC, requesting review and approval of the matter of "gratuitously transferring 20 million state-owned legal person shares held by Jilin Huaxing Electronics Group Co., Ltd. to Jilin City Small and Medium Enterprise Credit Guarantee Co., Ltd."

On December 2, 2008, the Jilin Provincial SASAC submitted a "Request for Submission and Approval of the Gratuitous Transfer of State-owned Legal Person Shares of Jilin Huaxing Electronics Group by Jilin City SASAC" (Jilin SASAC Report Property Rights (2008) No. 66) to the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council, requesting approval of the state-owned equity transfer by Jilin City SASAC.

On December 29, 2008, the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council issued a "Reply on Issues Concerning the Gratuitous Transfer of Shares Held by the State-owned Shareholder of Jilin Huamicro Electronics Co., Ltd." (State Assets Property Right (2008) No. 1439), approving the gratuitous transfer of 20 million shares of Huamicro Company held by Huaxing Company to SME Guarantee Company.

On January 15, 2009, the "Registration Confirmation of Transfer of Accounts at China Securities Depository and Clearing Corporation Limited Shanghai Branch" confirmed that "the transfer registration procedures for the above-mentioned gratuitous transfer of shares were completed on January 15, 2009."

On January 20, 2009, the board of directors of Huamicro Company issued a "Prompt Announcement on the Transfer of Accounts for Gratuitous Transfer of State-owned Shares" (Announcement No. Pro 2009-002), and published the announcement in the Shanghai Securities News on January 21, 2009.

On May 20, 2009, the Changchun Office of China Orient Asset Management Corporation transferred the above four debts together to Jilin Province State-owned Assets Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jilin Provincial State Assets Company).

On January 4, 2011, Jilin Provincial State Assets Company filed a lawsuit against Huaxing Company in the Jilin High People's Court, requesting that Huaxing Company perform its guarantee obligations for the above four debts (hereinafter referred to as the Huaxing Company Guarantee Liability Case).

On March 15, 2011, Jilin Provincial State Assets Company transferred the above four debts together to Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch. Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch then became the plaintiff in the Huaxing Company Guarantee Liability Case.

On April 15, 2011, Huaxing Company applied for bankruptcy to the Jilin High-tech Industrial Development Zone People's Court (hereinafter referred to as Jilin High-tech Zone Court). Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch declared its claims to the bankruptcy administrator of Huaxing Company according to law.

On August 24, 2011, the Jilin High-tech Zone Court issued a civil ruling (2011) Jilin Gaoxin Civil Bankruptcy Final No. 1-4, ordering the conclusion of the bankruptcy liquidation proceedings of Huaxing Company. In the bankruptcy liquidation process, the bankruptcy property of Huaxing Company was insufficient to satisfy the first-priority labor claims, with a shortfall of RMB 71,936,800. Since the Huaxing Company Guarantee Liability Case had not yet been concluded, the claim of Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch involved in that case was not recognized as an ordinary bankruptcy claim.

On May 13, 2013, the Jilin Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce issued a "Notice of Approval of Deregistration" (Ji He Zhu Tong Zhi Nei Zi (2013) No. 1300481950), approving the deregistration of Huaxing Company.

On December 11, 2013, the Jilin High People's Court rendered a civil judgment (2013) Jilin Civil First Instance No. 1 in the Huaxing Company Guarantee Liability Case, ruling that Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch held a guarantee claim against Huaxing Company for principal amounts of RMB 66.63 million and USD 4.8 million, plus interest of RMB 44,645,448.12 and USD 586,904.90. On December 27, 2014, this court rendered a civil judgment (2014) Supreme People's Court Final Civil No. 99, dismissing the appeal and upholding the original judgment.

Additionally, it was found that in March 2011, Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch had filed an action for creditor's avoidance against Huaxing Company and SME Guarantee Company in the Jilin High People's Court, seeking to revoke the share transfer agreement between Huaxing Company and SME Guarantee Company.

During the trial of that case, the Jilin Municipal People's Government issued a "Letter of Explanation on the Administrative Adjustment of Legal Person Shares of Jilin Huaxing Electronics Group Co., Ltd." (Jilin Municipal Government Letter (2011) No. 104) to the Jilin High People's Court, explaining the "administrative adjustment of the 20 million state-owned legal person shares held by Huaxing Company in that case as follows: First, the adjustment of the state-owned legal person shares was an administrative act of enterprise restructuring approved by three levels of government: Jilin City, Jilin Province, and the State Council. Second, according to Article 3 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Civil Disputes Related to Enterprise Restructuring, which states, 'If a dispute occurs during the administrative adjustment or transfer of state-owned assets by the competent government department, a party filing a civil lawsuit with a people's court shall not be accepted by the court,' the lawsuit filed by Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch should be handled in accordance with the above provisions."

The Jilin Higher People's Court rendered Civil Ruling (2011) Ji Min Er Chu Zi No. 1 on November 28, 2011, dismissing the lawsuit filed by Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch. Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch appealed against this ruling to the Supreme People's Court, which rendered Civil Ruling (2012) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 58 on August 5, 2013, holding that: "Although this transfer was approved by the Jilin Municipal People's Government and relevant departments, in essence, it was still a civil act of the Jilin Municipal SASAC, as the capital contributor, disposing of Huaxing Company's property, and disputes arising therefrom should be accepted as civil cases." "Since the Jilin High-tech Zone People's Court is the court handling the bankruptcy liquidation of Jilin Huaxing Electronics Group Co., Ltd., in accordance with Article 21 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that 'after a people's court accepts a bankruptcy application, civil actions concerning the debtor may only be brought before the people's court that accepted the bankruptcy application,' this case shall be accepted by the Jilin High-tech Zone People's Court as the court of first instance." The ruling set aside Civil Ruling (2011) Ji Min Er Chu Zi No. 1 and directed the Jilin High-tech Zone Court to accept the case as the court of first instance. During the proceedings before the Jilin High-tech Zone Court, Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch withdrew the lawsuit on January 28, 2015. The Jilin High-tech Zone Court rendered Civil Ruling (2014) Ji Gao Xin Min Er Chu Zi No. 129 on January 29, 2015, permitting the withdrawal of the lawsuit by Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch.

On the same day, Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch filed the present lawsuit with the court of first instance. The SME Guarantee Company applied to add Huaxing Company as a defendant in this case at the commencement of the first-instance trial but later withdrew that application on March 22, 2016.

The court of first instance held that, based on the plaintiff's claims and the defendant's defenses, the issues in dispute in this case were: 1. whether the SME Guarantee Company should bear joint and several liability to repay Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch within the scope of the 20 million shares it received; 2. whether Jilin Municipal SASAC should bear joint and several liability to discharge the debt within that scope; and 3. how to determine the cause of action in this case.

1. Regarding whether the SME Guarantee Company should bear joint and several liability to repay Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch within the scope of the 20 million shares it received: while Huaxing Company was bearing the guarantee liability, it transferred 20 million shares of Huawei Company held by it to the SME Guarantee Company without consideration. This factually resulted in a reduction of Huaxing Company's corporate property that served as security for the creditor. Moreover, neither Huaxing Company's transfer of shares without consideration nor the SME Guarantee Company's acceptance of shares without consideration dealt with Huaxing Company's existing debts, nor did they obtain the creditor's prior consent or subsequent ratification. This transfer without consideration infringed upon the creditor's rights and objectively caused the financial creditor's rights to become unenforceable. Pursuant to Article 106 of the General Principles of Civil Law, which provides that "a citizen or legal person who, through fault, infringes upon state or collective property or infringes upon the property or person of another shall bear civil liability," the SME Guarantee Company shall, within the scope of the benefit it received from the gratuitous acceptance of the 20 million shares of Huawei Company held by Huaxing Company, bear joint and several liability together with Huaxing Company to repay Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch for the principal and interest of the debt totaling RMB 209,240,000.

2. Regarding whether Jilin Municipal SASAC should bear joint and several liability to discharge the debt within that scope: Jilin Municipal SASAC is the state-owned assets supervision and administration institution established by the Jilin Municipal People's Government. In terms of performing its duties as a capital contributor for the management and supervision of state-owned assets, it enjoys the same legal status as a shareholder under company law. Article 20 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China may apply to disputes arising from the exercise of its rights as a capital contributor and the protection of creditors' interests. However, Article 20 of the Company Law is an equitable provision and may only be applied when the creditor's interests cannot be remedied through other means. In this case, the impact on the creditor's rights of Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch due to the exercise of rights by Jilin Municipal SASAC could be remedied by the SME Guarantee Company assuming liability for compensation based on the value of the shares it accepted. On this basis, Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch did not suffer losses due to the exercise of rights by Jilin Municipal SASAC, and there is no need to apply Article 20 of the Company Law to hold Jilin Municipal SASAC liable. Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch's request to hold Jilin Municipal SASAC jointly and severally liable on the grounds that it abused the independent legal personality of the company and the limited liability of shareholders lacks legal and factual basis; the court of first instance did not support it.

3. Regarding the cause of action in this case: Based on the first claim of Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch, it can be determined that the dispute between Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch and the SME Guarantee Company is a tort liability dispute. Based on the second claim of Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch, it can be determined that the dispute between Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch and Jilin Municipal SASAC is a dispute over liability for shareholders harming the interests of company creditors. Since this case involves multiple legal relationships, in accordance with Article 3(6) of the Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Revised Provisions on Causes of Action for Civil Cases (Fa [2011] No. 42), which provides that "if a single lawsuit involves two or more legal relationships, the cause of action shall be determined based on the nature of the legal relationship in dispute; if all are legal relationships in dispute, the causes of action shall be determined as parallel causes of action based on the two or more legal relationships in dispute," the causes of action in this case shall be determined as tort liability dispute and dispute over liability for shareholders harming the interests of company creditors.

The court of first instance ruled as follows: 1. The SME Guarantee Company shall, within the scope of the benefit it received from the gratuitous acceptance of the 20 million shares of Huawei Company held by Huaxing Company, bear joint and several liability to discharge the debt of RMB 209,240,000 in principal and interest owed by Huaxing Company to Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch; 2. Dismiss the other claims of Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch. The case acceptance fee of RMB 1,088,000 shall be borne by the SME Guarantee Company.

During the second-instance proceedings of this court, the parties submitted evidence in accordance with the law regarding their appeal claims. This court organized the parties to exchange evidence and cross-examine. The appellant SME Guarantee Company, during the trial, requested to supplement the facts found by the court of first instance, seeking to introduce records of creditors' meetings, showing that Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch had declared creditor's rights at two creditors' meetings, purportedly proving that the branch had participated in the bankruptcy proceedings as a bankruptcy creditor. However, the SME Guarantee Company did not submit the above materials as new evidence in the second-instance proceedings, nor did it submit them to this court. The fact that Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch had declared creditor's rights was already found in the first-instance judgment, and the parties had no dispute over it. Moreover, the above materials cannot prove that the creditor's rights of Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch were confirmed in the bankruptcy proceedings, and the purpose of the SME Guarantee Company's proof cannot be achieved; this court does not recognize it.

Jilin Municipal SASAC submitted five pieces of new evidence. Evidence 1: Business information of Huaxing Company; Evidence 2: Business information of Jilin Electronics State-owned Assets Management Company. The purpose of Evidence 1 and Evidence 2 is to prove that Jilin Municipal SASAC is not a shareholder of Huaxing Company. Evidence 3: Agreement on transfer of creditor's rights; Evidence 4: Business information of Jilin Provincial State-owned Assets Company and the approval for its establishment; Evidence 5: Request to approve Jilin Municipal SASAC's gratuitous transfer of Huaxing Company's state-owned legal person shares. The purpose of Evidence 3, Evidence 4, and Evidence 5 is to prove that, while Jilin Provincial State-owned Assets Company transferred state-owned assets to Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch, the latter's claim that the transfer was invalid and unreasonable is unfounded. The SME Guarantee Company raised no objections to the above evidence. The cross-examination opinion of Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch was: among the five pieces of evidence submitted by Jilin Municipal SASAC, Evidence 1 and Evidence 2 had not been seen before, and the authenticity of the above evidence could not be confirmed. Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch did not claim that the share transfer was invalid but rather requested the other party to assume joint and several liability. Evidence 3 to Evidence 5 cannot prove the purpose of Jilin Municipal SASAC's proof.

Regarding the evidence submitted by Jilin Municipal SASAC, this court finds as follows: As to Evidence 1 and Evidence 2, Jilin Municipal SASAC did not sufficiently explain the relevance of these materials to this case, and this court does not recognize them. Evidence 3 and Evidence 4 are copies; their authenticity cannot be confirmed and they are not relevant to the facts to be proved; they are not recognized. Evidence 5 was already submitted at the first-instance stage and does not constitute new evidence in the second-instance proceedings.

This court confirms the facts found by the court of first instance.

This court holds that, based on the appeal claims raised by the appellant and confirmed by both parties, the issues in dispute in the second-instance proceedings are: 1. Whether the first-instance procedure was illegal; 2. Whether the SME Guarantee Company should bear joint and several liability.

I. Whether the first-instance procedure was illegal

(1) Regarding the cause of action in this case

Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch filed the present lawsuit with the court of first instance against the SME Guarantee Company and Jilin Municipal SASAC as defendants, requesting: 1. The SME Guarantee Company, within the scope of the benefit it received from the gratuitous acceptance of the 20 million shares of Huawei Company held by Huaxing Company, bear joint and several liability together with Huaxing Company to repay Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch for the principal and interest of the debt; 2. Jilin Municipal SASAC, within the scope of the abuse of shareholder rights in gratuitously transferring the 20 million shares of Huawei Company held by Huaxing Company, bear joint and several liability together with Huaxing Company to repay Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch for the principal and interest of the debt. Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch brought the lawsuit based on the guarantee contract in which Huaxing Company was the debtor. When the court of first instance filed the case, it determined the cause of action as a contract dispute. During the first-instance trial, Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch changed its corresponding claims to: 1. The SME Guarantee Company, within the scope of the benefit it received from the gratuitous acceptance of the 20 million shares of Huawei Company held by Huaxing Company, bear joint and several liability to repay Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch for the principal and interest of the debt owed by Huaxing Company; 2. Jilin Municipal SASAC, within the scope of the abuse of shareholder rights in gratuitously transferring the 20 million shares of Huawei Company held by Huaxing Company, bear joint and several liability to repay Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch for the principal and interest of the debt owed by Huaxing Company. The reason was that Huaxing Company deliberately evaded debt by transferring the shares at issue to the SME Guarantee Company without consideration, and the SME Guarantee Company and Huaxing Company acted in malicious collusion, objectively causing the creditor's rights to become unenforceable, and therefore they should bear joint and several liability; Jilin Municipal SASAC abused the independent legal personality of the company and the limited liability of shareholders, assisting Huaxing Company in evading debt, seriously harming the interests of creditors, and should bear joint and several liability. Article 3(6) of the Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Revised Provisions on Causes of Action for Civil Cases provides that "if a party adds or changes its claims during the litigation, resulting in a change in the legal relationship in dispute between the parties, the people's court shall correspondingly change the cause of action." The cause of action is a summary and condensation of the legal relationship in dispute between the parties. The court of first instance, based on the changed claims of Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch, determined the nature of the legal relationship in dispute and set the causes of action as tort liability dispute and dispute over liability for shareholders harming the interests of company creditors, which was not improper.

(2) Regarding the litigation status of Huaxing Company in this case

On October 14, 2015, the SME Guarantee Company applied to the court of first instance to add Huaxing Company as a party to this case. During the trial, it insisted on adding Huaxing Company as a defendant. The plaintiff, Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch, stated that it had not filed a lawsuit against Huaxing Company, and since Huaxing Company's bankruptcy administrator had been dissolved, it did not agree to the addition. After the trial, the SME Guarantee Company submitted a written application to withdraw the request to add Huaxing Company as a defendant. The creditor's rights dispute between Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch and Huaxing Company had already been determined and resolved by the Supreme People's Court in another case (2014) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 99, a second-instance judgment. Before the present lawsuit was filed, the bankruptcy proceedings of Huaxing Company had been concluded, and its corporate registration had been cancelled. Huaxing Company's legal personality as a legal person had ceased to exist, and it lacked the capacity to be a party to the lawsuit. The court of first instance's failure to add Huaxing Company as a defendant was not improper.

II. Whether the SME Guarantee Company should bear joint and several liability

(1) Whether the guarantee creditor's rights enjoyed by Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch should be resolved under the Contract Law and the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law

1. The guarantee creditor's rights of Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch are lawful and valid. From 1997 to 2001, Huaxing Company provided guarantees for the loan debts of Gaote Company, Trauma Hospital, Semiconductor Branch, and Longding Group. After the guarantee contract took effect, the guarantor Huaxing Company was obligated to guarantee the debt and should perform it appropriately in accordance with the principle of good faith. On January 15, 2009, Huaxing Company gratuitously transferred the shares at issue to the SME Guarantee Company. On January 4, 2011, the guarantee creditor, Jilin Provincial State-owned Assets Company, sued Huaxing Company to assume the guarantee liability. Subsequently, Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch acquired the guarantee creditor's rights at issue from Jilin Provincial State-owned Assets Company, and after the transfer of the guarantee creditor's rights, it filed the lawsuit as the plaintiff. According to the facts found in the Supreme People's Court's judgment (2014) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 99, before the gratuitous transfer of the above shares, the creditor had asserted claims against both the principal debtor and Huaxing Company but failed to obtain satisfaction. That judgment found that Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch had guarantee creditor's rights against Huaxing Company. By the time that judgment became effective, Huaxing Company had been dissolved, and the guarantee creditor's rights at issue had not been satisfied.

2. The guarantee creditor's rights enjoyed by Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch were not included in the bankruptcy creditor's rights. On March 15, 2011, Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch acquired the guarantee creditor's rights at issue from Jilin Provincial State-owned Assets Company for consideration. The transfer of creditor's rights had been notified to the debtor Huaxing Company, and Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch had the right to assert creditor's rights against Huaxing Company. On April 15, 2011, Huaxing Company applied to the Jilin High-tech Zone Court for bankruptcy. On August 24, 2011, the Jilin High-tech Zone Court rendered a ruling (2011) Ji Gao Xin Min Po Zi No. 1-4, concluding the bankruptcy liquidation proceedings. Among the bankruptcy creditor's rights, the first priority was for unpaid labor remuneration owed by Huaxing Company; the creditor's rights of eight entities, including Jilin Jihua Chemical Products Sales Office, were ordinary bankruptcy creditor's rights. The guarantee creditor's rights at issue belonging to Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch were not included in the bankruptcy creditor's rights. Article 44 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law provides: "Creditors who have creditor's rights against the debtor at the time of the acceptance of the bankruptcy application by the people's court shall exercise their rights in accordance with the procedures provided by this Law." Article 48 provides: "Creditors shall, within the period for declaring creditor's rights determined by the people's court, declare their creditor's rights to the administrator." Article 57 provides: "After receiving the materials for declaring creditor's rights, the administrator shall register them in a ledger, examine the declared creditor's rights, and prepare a schedule of creditor's rights." After the acceptance of Huaxing Company's bankruptcy application, Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch declared its creditor's rights to the bankruptcy administrator in accordance with the law. However, the bankruptcy administrator did not list Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch as a bankruptcy creditor. Due to reasons not attributable to itself, Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch was unable to participate in the distribution of bankruptcy assets. Moreover, the bankruptcy liquidation proceedings had already concluded, and its guarantee creditor's rights could not be remedied through bankruptcy proceedings. The SME Guarantee Company's appeal argument that Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch was a bankruptcy creditor of Huaxing Company and should exercise its rights in accordance with the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law is untenable.

3. The shares at issue do not constitute property that the creditor, Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch, could request to be additionally distributed after the conclusion of Huaxing Company's bankruptcy proceedings. Article 123 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law provides: "Within two years from the date of conclusion of the bankruptcy proceedings in accordance with Article 43, paragraph 4, or Article 120 of this Law, if any of the following circumstances exist, a creditor may request the people's court to make an additional distribution in accordance with the plan for distribution of bankruptcy assets: (1) property is discovered that should be recovered under Articles 31, 32, 33, or 36 of this Law; (2) other property that the bankrupt should have distributed is discovered." The shares at issue can no longer be additionally distributed to creditors in accordance with the plan for distribution of bankruptcy assets. First, the shares at issue were transferred to the SME Guarantee Company on January 15, 2009. At the time of Huaxing Company's bankruptcy application and after acceptance until the conclusion of the bankruptcy proceedings, the shares at issue were not included in the scope of Huaxing Company's debtor's property, and Article 33 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law is not applicable. Second, Huaxing Company entered bankruptcy proceedings two years after the transfer of the shares at issue. The bankruptcy administrator did not request to revoke and recover the shares at issue in accordance with Article 31 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law, nor did the situation fall under Articles 32 or 36 of the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law. Third, regarding the two-year period for recovery: the SME Guarantee Company did not provide evidence that, when Huaxing Company gratuitously transferred the shares at issue, it notified the creditor. The creditor was entitled to exercise its right of revocation under the Contract Law within one year from the date it knew or should have known of the grounds for revocation. In March 2011, Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch sued Huaxing Company and the SME Guarantee Company before the Jilin Higher People's Court, seeking to revoke the gratuitous transfer of the shares at issue. The Jilin Higher People's Court ruled to dismiss the lawsuit. On August 5, 2013, the Supreme People's Court, in Civil Ruling (2012) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 58, set aside the first-instance ruling and directed the Jilin High-tech Zone Court to hear the case. When the Jilin High-tech Zone Court accepted the case on July 3, 2014, more than two years had elapsed since the conclusion of Huaxing Company's bankruptcy liquidation. Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch could hardly obtain relief for its rights under the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law.

In summary, the SME Guarantee Company's appeal argument that Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch should assert its rights in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Contract Law and the Enterprise Bankruptcy Law is untenable.

(2) Whether the SME Guarantee Company should bear tort liability

According to the claims and reasons of Great Wall Asset Management Co., Jilin Branch, its primary request is for the SME Guarantee Company to bear tort liability. Generally speaking, creditor's rights arise between specific parties and lack publicity. Third parties often cannot foresee them, and they are typically not within the scope of protection under tort law. Of course, the Tort Liability Law does not exclude creditor's rights from its scope of protection. Therefore, the protection of creditor's rights is primarily achieved through legal systems such as contract law. If a third party other than the contracting party is to be found liable for tortious compensation, the standard should be strictly applied.

1. Whether SME Guarantee Company had subjective fault. According to the facts found at first instance, on January 16, 2006, Huaxing Company submitted a request to Jilin SASAC, because Huaxing Company was insolvent, applying for restructuring. The plan was that Huaxing Company would transfer the equity involved in the case to the Jilin Municipal People's Government for disposition, and the Jilin Municipal People's Government would be responsible for receiving and arranging for the employees of Huaxing Company. Jilin SASAC approved and made a recommendation to the Jilin Municipal People's Government to transfer the equity involved in the case free of charge to SME Guarantee Company. Therefore, the above plan for the gratuitous transfer of equity was part of the restructuring plan of Huaxing Company. The Notice on Opinions on Regulating the Reform of State-owned Enterprises and the Notice on Implementation Opinions on Further Regulating the Reform of State-owned Enterprises issued by the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council clearly emphasize that during the restructuring of enterprises, financial claims must be preserved and financial debts must be settled to prevent using enterprise restructuring to evade financial debts. Although the gratuitous transfer of the equity involved in the case was formally approved by the Jilin Municipal People's Government and its relevant departments, in substance, Jilin SASAC performed its duties as the contributor, and the restructuring entity Huaxing Company gratuitously transferred state-owned assets to SME Guarantee Company, with the three parties cooperating to implement the restructuring plan. Article 30 of the Enterprise State-owned Assets Law of the PRC provides, "In major matters such as merger, division, restructuring, listing, increase or decrease of registered capital, issuance of bonds, making major investments, providing large guarantees for others, transferring major property, making large donations, distributing profits, and dissolution or application for bankruptcy, state-invested enterprises shall comply with the provisions of laws, administrative regulations, and the company's articles of association, and shall not harm the rights and interests of contributors and creditors." The disposition of the equity involved in the case by Huaxing Company during the restructuring process constituted a gratuitous transfer of major property by a state-owned enterprise, and is legally prohibited from harming the legitimate rights and interests of creditors. Article 6 of the Interim Measures for the Management of Gratuitous Transfers of State-owned Property Rights of Enterprises, promulgated and implemented by the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission of the State Council on August 29, 2005, provides, "A feasibility study shall be conducted for the gratuitous transfer of state-owned property rights of enterprises. A feasibility report for a gratuitous transfer shall generally include the following contents ... (3) the financial status and contingent liabilities of the enterprise whose property rights are being transferred." Article 7 provides, "Both parties to the transfer shall, on the basis of the feasibility study, deliberate in accordance with the internal decision-making procedures and form a written resolution." Article 8 provides, "The transferring party shall notify the creditors of its enterprise (unit) of the gratuitous transfer and formulate a corresponding debt settlement plan." The above regulatory documents clearly stipulate that the transferring party shall notify creditors of a gratuitous transfer. As the transferring party, Huaxing Company should have formulated a debt settlement and transfer plan in accordance with the regulations. As the receiving party, SME Guarantee Company should have studied, deliberated, and formed a written resolution. When Huaxing Company requested the gratuitous transfer of the equity assets involved in the case from the relevant government departments, the enterprise was already insolvent. SME Guarantee Company knew or should have foreseen this. Article 5 of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides, "The lawful civil rights and interests of citizens and legal persons shall be protected by law, and no organization or individual may infringe upon them." The guaranteed creditor's rights of Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch are property rights and interests lawfully enjoyed by the creditor and are protected by law. In a creditor-debt relationship, the debtor shall follow the principle of good faith, perform contractual obligations, and actively promote the realization of debt repayment. At the same time, third parties other than the debtor shall also act in good faith towards legally established and effective creditor's rights and shall not arbitrarily infringe upon them. Huaxing Company, being insolvent and on the verge of bankruptcy, gratuitously transferred the equity involved in the case to others, which demonstrated subjective intent to evade debts. SME Guarantee Company failed to provide evidence proving that it paid reasonable consideration for obtaining the equity property. SME Guarantee Company's cooperation with Huaxing Company in evading debts violated legal and regulatory provisions, contravened public order and good customs, and constituted subjective fault in infringing upon the property rights of others. At first instance and on appeal, SME Guarantee Company and Jilin SASAC argued that the transfer of the equity involved in the case was nominally gratuitous but actually for consideration, and that the consideration received by SME Guarantee Company for the equity transfer was the government's arrangement of Huaxing Company's employees at a cost exceeding RMB 200 million, but neither provided evidence to support this. Furthermore, SME Guarantee Company and Jilin SASAC also argued that over RMB 70 million in first-priority labor claims of Huaxing Company had not been satisfied, and the first-instance judgment would trigger employee rights protection. SME Guarantee Company's statements regarding whether consideration was paid for receiving the equity were inconsistent, and this Court does not accept them. SME Guarantee Company's ground of appeal that it was not at fault for gratuitously receiving the equity involved in the case cannot be established.

2. The act of gratuitously transferring the equity involved in the case directly harmed the property interests of Huaxing Company's creditors. Huaxing Company entered bankruptcy proceedings immediately after transferring the equity involved in the case to SME Guarantee Company. The ruling (2011) Ji Gao Xin Min Po Zi No. 1-4 of the Jilin High-tech Zone People's Court found that, as of August 23, 2011, according to the verification by the bankruptcy administrator, Huaxing Company's bankruptcy estate consisted only of 4 vehicles, 3 computers, and cash of RMB 3,221,200, totaling RMB 3,718,600, which was insufficient to satisfy even the first-priority labor compensation claims. The gratuitous transfer and receipt of the equity involved in the case objectively led to a reduction in Huaxing Company's solvency, and there is a direct causal link between this and the failure to realize the guaranteed creditor's rights involved in the case. The guaranteed creditor's rights acquired by Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch through the transfer of non-performing assets could not, under the contract-based debt approach such as the Guarantee Law or Contract Law, break the relativity of contracts to assert claims against a third party other than the contractual counterparty, namely SME Guarantee Company, which had received the property gratuitously. Accordingly, based on the actual circumstances of this case, it is necessary to apply tort liability law as a supplementary means to protect property rights and interests; otherwise, creditors with legitimate property rights and interests would find it difficult to obtain relief through statutory channels, which would be contrary to fairness and justice.

In summary, because SME Guarantee Company acted with fault in cooperating with Huaxing Company to transfer the equity involved in the case, and its gratuitous receipt of the equity involved in the case infringed upon the legitimate property rights and interests of Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch, in accordance with Article 106 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, which provides, "A citizen or legal person who, through fault, infringes upon state property or collective property, or infringes upon the property or person of another person, shall bear civil liability," SME Guarantee Company shall bear civil liability.

3. The assertion of rights by Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch against SME Guarantee Company does not violate the principle of fair satisfaction of claims. Since acquiring the guaranteed creditor's rights involved in the case, Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch has sought remedies through multiple channels. First, Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch asserted its rights in the case where Jilin Provincial State-owned Assets Company sued the principal debtor and Huaxing Company to fulfill the guarantee obligation. However, because Huaxing Company had entered bankruptcy proceedings, that case only confirmed Huaxing Company's guarantee obligations and did not order Huaxing Company to perform the guarantee. Second, after Huaxing Company entered bankruptcy proceedings, Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch actively filed its claims but, for reasons not attributable to itself, was not included as a bankruptcy creditor, and its efforts to obtain relief through bankruptcy proceedings were unsuccessful. Third, almost simultaneously with acquiring the guaranteed creditor's rights involved in the case, Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch also exercised the creditor's right of revocation with respect to the gratuitous transfer of the equity involved in the case. However, because, by the time the Supreme People's Court concluded the second instance of that case and the Jilin High-tech Zone People's Court accepted the case for substantive trial, more than two years had elapsed since the conclusion of Huaxing Company's bankruptcy proceedings, the equity involved in the case could no longer be subject to additional distribution, and this effort also failed. In summary, Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch initiated this property tort litigation because its avenues for rights relief were essentially exhausted; it did not neglect to assert contractual rights or circumvent bankruptcy proceedings to seek individual satisfaction or priority. SME Guarantee Company's argument that the individual satisfaction of Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch's ordinary claim infringed upon the property rights and interests of other creditors of Huaxing Company cannot be established.

(3) The first-instance judgment ordering SME Guarantee Company to bear joint and several liability is insufficiently grounded

It is difficult to find in this case that SME Guarantee Company and Huaxing Company constituted a joint tort. Article 130 of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides that where two or more persons jointly cause damage to others through their tort, they shall bear joint and several liability. On November 18, 2008, Jilin SASAC submitted to Jilin Provincial SASAC a "Request for Gratuitously Transferring the State-owned Legal Person Shares of Jilin Huaxing Electronics Group Co., Ltd. to Jilin City SME Credit Guarantee Company," which stated that the transfer of the equity involved in the case was intended to "further enhance the strength of SME Guarantee Company and provide a financing platform for the development of small and medium-sized enterprises in Jilin City." Therefore, the gratuitous transfer of the equity involved in the case occurred against the background of state-owned enterprise restructuring and was completed under the guidance and approval of the competent government authorities. As a state-invested enterprise, SME Guarantee Company's acceptance of the equity involved in the case involved a degree of passivity and did not have the subjective intent, through a meeting of minds with Huaxing Company, to jointly infringe upon the property rights and interests of others. Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch did not submit sufficient evidence to prove that Huaxing Company and SME Guarantee Company constituted a joint tort. Therefore, the first-instance judgment ordering SME Guarantee Company to bear joint and several liability was improper, and this Court corrects it.

(4) SME Guarantee Company shall bear corresponding compensation liability

In January 2009, the equity involved in the case was gratuitously transferred from Huaxing Company to SME Guarantee Company. At that time, the creditors, China Orient Asset Management Corporation Changchun Office and Jilin Provincial State-owned Assets Company, could have but failed to closely monitor the major asset changes of the debtor Huaxing Company. All of the above facts occurred before Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch acquired the guaranteed creditor's rights involved in the case. The debtor's solvency, the creditor's knowledge and grasp of defects in the rights, and other circumstances can affect the realization of creditor's rights. Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch, as a corporate legal person specialized in the acquisition and disposal of non-performing claims, should have possessed professional verification and judgment capabilities regarding the risks of realizing the acquired claims. The actions of China Orient Asset Management Corporation Changchun Office and Jilin Provincial State-owned Assets Company led to increased difficulties and risks in subsequently realizing the guaranteed creditor's rights involved in the case, and they also had fault, the legal consequences of which shall be borne by the creditor's assignee, Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch. Article 131 of the General Principles of the Civil Law provides, "If the victim is also at fault for the occurrence of the damage, the civil liability of the tortfeasor may be reduced." Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch cannot claim the entire loss within the scope of the equity gratuitously received by SME Guarantee Company. Furthermore, taking into account factors such as SME Guarantee Company's performance of shareholder duties after receiving the equity involved in the case and the relative passivity of SME Guarantee Company in receiving the equity involved in the case, this Court deems it appropriate to order SME Guarantee Company to bear corresponding compensation liability within the scope of 80% of the value of the equity it gratuitously received.

Great Wall Asset Company Jilin Branch's claim sought joint and several liability from SME Guarantee Company. SME Guarantee Company appealed arguing that it should not bear civil liability. This Court considers that the first-instance judgment ordering SME Guarantee Company to bear joint and several liability was improper. Given that both joint and several liability and compensation liability are forms of liability for tort, and without prejudice to the characterization of the dispute in this case, in accordance with the principle of convenience, this Court renders an amended judgment according to law.

In conclusion, the first-instance judgment was improper and this Court corrects it. Pursuant to Articles 106 and 131 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, and Article 170, Paragraph 1, Item 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, this Court hereby renders the following judgment:

1. Set aside the civil judgment (2015) Ji Min Er Chu Zi No. 8 of the Jilin High People's Court;

2. Jilin City SME Credit Guarantee Group Co., Ltd. shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, bear compensation liability for the principal and interest of the debt of RMB 209,240,000 owed by Jilin Huaxing Electronics Group Co., Ltd. to China Great Wall Asset Management Co., Ltd., Jilin Branch, within the scope of the benefits derived from the 16 million shares of Jilin Huamai Microelectronics Co., Ltd. held by Jilin Huaxing Electronics Group Co., Ltd. that it gratuitously received;

3. Dismiss the other claims of China Great Wall Asset Management Co., Ltd., Jilin Branch.

If the obligation to pay money is not performed within the period specified in this judgment, the interest on the debt during the period of delayed performance shall be doubled in accordance with Article 253 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC.

Court acceptance fee for the first instance: RMB 1,088,000. Jilin City SME Credit Guarantee Group Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 870,400, and China Great Wall Asset Management Co., Ltd., Jilin Branch shall bear RMB 217,600. Court acceptance fee for the second instance: RMB 1,088,000. Jilin City SME Credit Guarantee Group Co., Ltd. shall bear RMB 870,400, and China Great Wall Asset Management Co., Ltd., Jilin Branch shall bear RMB 217,600.

This judgment is final.
